title: SecOps-NG Incidents Evidence Artifact
description: Typed shape for one evidence artifact emitted by the incidents evidence stream (F-CP-02). One artifact is produced per (incident_id, execution_id) — one cycle of the F-WF-05 incident-management workflow over one incident case — and carries the NIS2 Article 23(3) significance classification, the lifecycle markers feeding the MTTD / MTTR / containment-window / eradication-window KPIs, and the NIS2 Article 23(4) regulator-notification milestones reached so far. Downstream consumers are `kpi.mttd@v1`, `kpi.mttr@v1`, `kpi.mttr_critical@v1`, `kpi.mttr_containment@v1`, `kpi.timeline_completeness@v1`, `kpi.notification_sla_compliance@v1`, `kri.regulator_notification_overrun@v1`, plus the NIS2 Article 23 milestone KPIs (`kpi.early_warning_on_time@v1`, `kpi.notification_72h_on_time@v1`, `kpi.final_report_on_time@v1`) once they land in `content/metrics/`. Public-bar artifact: operator-side strings (owner labels, submission references) MUST stay role-shaped or URN-shaped; individual personal names are out of scope per AGENTS.md §3.

schema_version.description: Pinned schema version. Lets a consumer reject artifacts produced under an older schema once breaking changes ship.

artifact_id.description: Stable per-artifact identifier. Convention: SHA-256 hex digest of `<incident_id>|<execution_id>` (UTF-8, no separators around the pipe). Deterministic on those two inputs so a replay of the same execution re-derives the same id and dedup is trivial.

stream.description: Identifies which evidence stream produced the artifact. Constant on this schema.

incident_id.description: Stable case identifier for the incident as a UUID (RFC 4122). Issued upstream by the F-WF-05 timeline-open primitive (`primitives/timeline_binding.open_timeline`) so every re-execution of the same incident across the lifecycle pins against one id.

execution_id.description: Per-execution identifier issued by the compile target's workflow runtime (n8n execution id, Temporal workflow run id, LangGraph thread/checkpoint id). Re-runs of the same incident_id produce distinct execution_ids — the regulator-notification chain treats re-emission as evidentiary signal rather than dedup waste.

regulation_refs.description: Pins to the upstream regulatory mapping entries this artifact helps satisfy (e.g. nis2:art-21-2-b, nis2:art-23-early-warning, nis2:art-23-notification-72h, nis2:art-23-final-report). At least one entry — an artifact with no regulatory anchor is not evidence in the F-CP-02 sense. Joins back into content/mappings/<regime>/*.yaml via the `id` field.

control_refs.description: Control stable-ids attested by this artifact. Same shape every other layer of the content model uses. At least one — typically `control.incident_handling_capability@v1` and/or `control.incident_timeline_signals@v1`.

classification.description: Deterministic outputs of the F-WF-05 classify-significance primitive (`primitives/classification.py`). The `significant` and `cross_border` booleans and the ordered `reasons` list are reproduced verbatim from the `ClassificationVerdict` dataclass; the `rule_ids` field pins the policy rows that fired so a replay-vs-original comparison is single-string-equal. Free-text narrative for the incident stays in `summary` (filled by the F-WF-05 final-report DSPy signature, per `primitives/signatures.py`).

significant.description: NIS2 Article 23(3) significance flag. When false the workflow takes the intake-only audit-close branch and most downstream fields (notification_timeline, severity, KPI windows) will be empty or short.

reasons.description: Ordered list of human-readable rule-reason strings from the classification verdict. Public-bar text: no operator branding, no individual names.

rule_ids.description: Ordered list of policy rule ids (e.g. `sig.severe_disruption`, `cb.multi_member_state`) that fired in the classification verdict. Pins behaviour against `classification_policy.yaml` so a replay diff is a single-string check.

severity.description: Optional operator-graded incident severity band the response chain reads. Closed five-band alphabet matching the CVSS qualitative vocabulary the vulns stream uses so downstream consumers consume one alphabet across streams.

summary.description: One-paragraph plain-language summary of the incident. Public-bar text: no operator branding, no individual names. Typically filled by the F-WF-05 final-report DSPy signature.

lifecycle.description: Lifecycle-marker timestamps the catalog KPIs measure against. Each marker is the canonical event time per `kpi.mttd@v1`, `kpi.mttr_containment@v1`, `kpi.timeline_completeness@v1`, and the post-incident review formulas. All markers ISO-8601 UTC. `detected_at` is required (the incident exists from the detection instant); the remainder are optional while the incident is open and required once the incident is closed (downstream completeness KPI reads against the present set).

first_observation_at.description: Earliest event in the telemetry stream that, in hindsight, was part of the incident's causal chain. Bound at evaluation time by the post-incident review timeline, not at detection time. Head of the `kpi.mttd@v1` interval.

detected_at.description: First authoritative detection firing that opened the incident record. Head of `kpi.mttr_critical@v1` and `kpi.mttr_containment@v1`; tail of `kpi.mttd@v1`.

triaged_at.description: Triage-complete timestamp (the F-WF-05 classify-significance primitive's verdict instant). Optional; carried for analyst-handoff analyses.

contained_at.description: First containment action recorded in the response playbook (the canonical `containment` step). Tail of `kpi.mttr_critical@v1` and `kpi.mttr_containment@v1`; head of the `containment_window` measurement.

eradicated_at.description: Eradication-complete timestamp (the threat actor / root cause removed). Tail of the `containment_window` measurement; head of the `eradication_window` measurement.

recovered_at.description: Service-recovery timestamp (operational state restored). Tail of the `eradication_window` measurement.

closed_at.description: Incident-record closeout timestamp (lessons-learned captured, post-incident review filed). Read by `kpi.timeline_completeness@v1` and `kri.incidents_without_closeout@v1`.

kpi_windows.description: Optional pre-computed KPI windows the emitter may carry so downstream rollups skip re-derivation. The catalog KPIs may compute these themselves from `lifecycle`; the fields reserve the shape for emitters that already track them. All values in minutes (matches the catalog `unit: minutes`).

mttd_minutes.description: (detected_at - first_observation_at) in minutes. Consumed by `kpi.mttd@v1`. Non-negative.

mttr_minutes.description: (contained_at - detected_at) in minutes. Consumed by `kpi.mttr@v1` and `kpi.mttr_critical@v1` (when classification.severity == 'Critical'). Non-negative.

containment_window_minutes.description: (eradicated_at - contained_at) in minutes. Reserves the shape for the planned `kpi.containment_window@v1` catalog entry. Non-negative.

eradication_window_minutes.description: (recovered_at - eradicated_at) in minutes. Reserves the shape for the planned `kpi.eradication_window@v1` catalog entry. Non-negative.

notification_timeline.description: Ordered list of NIS2 Article 23(4) regulator-notification milestones the case has reached. Empty array is valid — a `classification.significant == false` case carries no milestones. Each entry is read by the per-milestone KPIs (`kpi.early_warning_on_time@v1`, `kpi.notification_72h_on_time@v1`, `kpi.final_report_on_time@v1`) to compute the on-time ratio against the milestone's declared deadline. Records are append-only across executions for the same incident_id.

milestone.description: Which NIS2 Article 23(4) milestone this entry records. Imports the shared vocabulary from schemas/nis2_incident_notification_milestone.json.

clock_started_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp at which the clock for this milestone started — the operator's awareness instant on the incident (typically `lifecycle.detected_at`, or the F-WF-05 `timeline_open` instant which the workflow pins them to).

submitted_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp at which the notification or report was submitted to the CSIRT / competent authority (or the closest evidentiary equivalent).

submission_ref.description: Operator-side opaque reference for the submission (CSIRT ticket id, regulator portal receipt id, URN). Free-text constrained — no commentary, no operator branding.

on_time.description: Optional pre-computed on-time flag (clock_started_at + deadline ≥ submitted_at). The catalog KPIs may compute this themselves; the field reserves the shape for emitters that already track it.

owner.description: Dated ownership pointer required by NIS2 Art. 21(2)(b) (`incident-handling capability`). Role-shaped — a working-group mailbox, a generic role title, or a community handle. Individual personal names are out of scope per AGENTS.md §3 and rejected here as a matter of schema discipline.

role.description: Generic role or working-group identifier (e.g. 'csirt@example.org', 'incident-commander', 'soc-on-call'). Personal names are not used.

assigned_at.description: ISO-8601 date on which the role was assigned ownership of this incident.

captured_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp at which this artifact was captured. Stable input to the emitter's per-execution dedup decision; not part of artifact_id (which is derived from incident_id + execution_id so re-emissions in the same execution stay byte-identical).

provenance.description: Where this artifact came from. Mirrors the provenance pattern used by content/controls/*.yaml so a reviewer can re-derive the chain back to source.

source_url.description: URL of the workflow run (or workflow-content source) that produced this artifact. Compile targets may use their own run-id URLs; the URL itself is opaque to this schema.

captured_at.description: ISO-8601 date or date-time matching the artifact-level captured_at.

commit_sha.description: Optional commit SHA of the content snapshot the workflow walked.

retention.description: Optional retention pointer the operator declares for this evidentiary record. ISO-8601 duration, defaulted by the operator's configuration. Schema reserves the field; the community-default value is an open question to be settled with the EXTEND-NIS2-MAPPING card.
